source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.exact_claim: The original linear word contains a contiguous subword s that is an initial segment of a symmetrised defining relator r with |s| > |r|/2; the proof obtains it from a shell whose exterior arc is longer than half the face boundary.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.kind: TikZ van Kampen shell / Greendlinger overlap schematic
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.why_warranted: The stated conclusion is precisely the long boundary overlap of a relator face, and the proof derives it by comparing the exterior arc with at most three short internal arcs.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.specific_content_maps_relations_to_draw_: Draw a single polygonal face with its cyclic boundary labelled by a chosen symmetrised relator r. Mark the exterior arc s as a contiguous segment of the original outer boundary and show |s|>|r|/2. Partition the complementary inner boundary into i∈{1,2,3} maximal internal arcs, each shorter than |r|/6. Orient the cyclic face reading so s is an initial segment of r; do not reverse only one of the boundary labels or imply arbitrary signed relators beyond symmetrisation.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; all labels and inequalities follow from source lines 27, 33, 35, 43, 45, while correctness is already stated and proved in prose.

source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.exact_claim: A finite group acting on a simplicial tree fixes a vertex after barycentric subdivision; the proof takes the midpoint of a diameter in a finite invariant subtree and, when the diameter is odd, uses the no-inversions action to fix both endpoints of its midpoint edge.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.kind: TikZ tree subdivision and diameter-midpoint schematic
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.why_warranted: The distinction between an edge midpoint in the subdivided tree and the two fixed endpoints in the odd-diameter case is central to the claim and easy to confuse in prose.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.specific_content_maps_relations_to_draw_: Use two labeled panels: in T, show a finite group element swapping endpoints of an edge; in T′, insert the barycentric midpoint and show it fixed. A second compact tree panel may mark an odd-length diameter x–m–y, with m the midpoint vertex of T′, or its corresponding stabilized edge before subdivision. Keep the action and fixed-point labels exact; do not claim the original T has a fixed vertex when it only preserves an edge.
source_supported_missing_diagram_candida.certainty: uncertain optional candidate; the midpoint and no-inversions argument are explicit at lines 38, 48, 50, and the proof does not require a figure.
